module purpose: neorv32_cpu_frontend sequences instruction fetches: it stores fetch/restart state, a fetch PC and privilege, drives instruction-bus requests, packs acknowledged bus responses into a two-lane prefetch buffer, and outputs instruction, valid/compressed/fault, and halted status to the next CPU stage. When RVC_EN is true it also tracks halfword alignment and uses a decompressor for 16-bit instructions.

use-case flows.value: fetch sequencing, restart control, fetch PC update, and fetch privilege capture
instruction-bus request generation from the stored fetch context, with request strobe only when the frontend is in request state and both prefetch lanes are free
packing an acknowledged bus response into two 17-bit prefetch-buffer entries and writing them into the two FIFO lanes
when RVC_EN is true, selecting the aligned 16-bit halfword, optionally decompressing it, assembling a 32-bit instruction, updating alignment, and consuming the required buffer lane or lanes
when RVC_EN is false, consuming both buffer lanes on if_ack and presenting the concatenated 32-bit instruction
issued instruction word and its valid/compressed/fault qualifiers on frontend_o
halted status when a fetch request is blocked because the prefetch buffer is not fully free
fetch state, restart flag, fetch PC, fetch privilege, and compressed-issue alignment forced to reset values

conceptual assets.concept: Fetch-control sequencing state and pending restart/flush decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: The fetch FSM stores both `fetch.state` and `fetch.restart`: `fetch.restart` accumulates `ctrl_i.if_reset` in request and pending states (lines 91, 100), state transitions are decided at lines 92-107, and the restart branch clears `fetch.restart` and re-enters request mode at lines 113-116. These stored control values directly govern request strobing (line 124), halted reporting (line 145), FIFO clearing through `clear_i => fetch.restart` (line 164), and issue alignment re-seeding (lines 205-206). Integrity is established because the implemented fetch sequencing and flush behavior depends on these exact state values; availability is also established because progression through restart/request/pending is explicitly encoded in the same lines.

The stored fetch address is initialized from `ctrl_i.pc_nxt` in the restart branch (line 114) and, after an acknowledged pending fetch, it advances by 4 and forces bit 1 low (lines 102-103). This state drives the request address at line 123 and also affects which prefetch-buffer lane is written at line 141 through `fetch.pc(1)`. Integrity is established because both the address sent to the instruction bus and the lane-placement rule follow these update equations. The instruction-bus request record itself is transport and is therefore not listed as an exit port.

On restart, the frontend captures `ctrl_i.cpu_priv` into `fetch.priv` (line 115) and later copies that stored value onto the request privilege field (line 129). Integrity is established because the external consumer of the fetch request must receive the privilege value defined by this flow. The instruction-bus request record is transport and therefore omitted from the structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Prefetch-buffer instruction halfwords with attached fault flag
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each acknowledged bus response is repacked into two 17-bit values, `ibus_rsp_i.err & ibus_rsp_i.data(15 downto 0)` and `ibus_rsp_i.err & ibus_rsp_i.data(31 downto 16)` (lines 137-138), then written into the two FIFO lanes through `wdata_i` and `we_i` (lines 168-169, with write enables at lines 141-142). Later issue logic uses the buffered values to form `frontend_o.instr` and `frontend_o.fault` (lines 220-245, 267-270). Integrity is established because the later instruction and fault report depend on these stored halfwords and error bits. Storage itself is inside the instantiated FIFO, so this module exposes the value only where it computes the FIFO input.

When `RVC_EN` is true, `issue.algn` is reset to `'0'` (line 203), re-seeded from `ctrl_i.pc_nxt(1)` on fetch restart (lines 205-206), and otherwise updated on `ctrl_i.if_ack` by `(issue.algn and (not issue.aclr)) or issue.aset` (lines 207-208). This stored state selects which halfword becomes `issue.cmd16` (line 195), which buffered fault bit and instruction assembly path drive `frontend_o` (lines 219-246), and which FIFO lane or lanes are consumed through `issue.ack` and `ipb.re` (lines 223, 228, 238, 243, 252-253). Integrity is established because corrupting the alignment state misselects instruction bits and buffer consumption. When `RVC_EN` is false, line 261 ties `issue.algn` to `'0'`, so the variable alignment state exists only in the RVC-enabled build.

conceptual assets.concept: Issued instruction word delivered to the backend
conceptual assets.reasoning: In the RVC-enabled build, the selected 16-bit halfword is sent to the decompressor (line 190) and the decompressed 32-bit result returns on `issue.cmd32` (line 191), which is then used for compressed instructions at lines 225 and 240. For 32-bit instructions, the frontend concatenates buffered halfwords directly at lines 230 and 245, and without RVC it always concatenates both lanes at line 268. Integrity is established because the consumer on `frontend_o` must receive exactly the instruction word selected by these implemented alignment and length rules.

`frontend_o.valid` is asserted only when the required buffered word or words are available: in the RVC-enabled build at lines 224, 229, 239 and 244, depending on alignment and whether the selected halfword encodes a compressed or 32-bit instruction, and in the non-RVC build at line 267. Integrity is established because downstream logic must only accept an instruction when the frontend indicates validity under those exact RTL-visible conditions. Availability is also established conditionally on `ipb.avail` under the same predicates.

When `RVC_EN` is true, the frontend reports whether the issued instruction came from a 16-bit compressed encoding: `frontend_o.compr <= '1'` in the compressed cases at lines 226 and 241, and `<= '0'` in the 32-bit cases at lines 231 and 246. When `RVC_EN` is false, line 269 ties the report low. Integrity is established because the backend consumer must receive the implemented compressed/not-compressed indication that matches the selected instruction path.

The frontend reports the stored error flag from the selected buffer lane as `frontend_o.fault`: from lane 0 at line 220, from lane 1 at line 235 when RVC alignment selects that lane, and from lane 0 again in the non-RVC build at line 270. Integrity is established because the consumer of `frontend_o` must receive the fault indication associated with the fetched instruction source actually used by this logic.

The frontend reports itself halted only under the explicit predicate `fetch.state = S_REQUEST` and `ipb.free /= "11"` (line 145), meaning a new fetch request is pending but the two prefetch lanes are not fully free. Integrity is established because external control using this status depends on that exact condition. Availability is also established whenever those visible RTL conditions hold.
